title: Windows Update Failed
cardText: Diagnose Windows updates that fail to download, install or complete.
Investigate error codes, update services, storage, download cache and Windows component corruption.
Use targeted repairs and Windows recovery options before considering a reinstall.
text: This guide covers Windows Update failures, repeated installation errors and updates stuck during downloading or installation.
Begin with the exact error code, failing update and installation history.
Use Windows Update diagnostics before resetting services or changing system components.
Investigate update cache, system files and installation logs if the problem persists.
Back up important data before major Windows recovery operations.

checkErrorMessage.title: Identify the Windows Update failure
body: Open Settings, Windows Update, Update history.
Identify the failed update, its KB number and any displayed error code.
Record whether the failure occurs during downloading, installation or after restarting.
Examples of Windows Update error codes include 0x80070002, 0x80070005, 0x800f081f and 0x8024402c.
Different error codes have different causes, so avoid applying unrelated fixes.
If no error code is displayed, continue with the general update diagnostics.

link.name: Microsoft: Troubleshoot Windows Update
link.description: Official guidance for Windows Update installation failures and error codes.

checkUpdateType.title: Determine which updates are failing
body: Check whether one specific KB update is failing or several unrelated updates cannot install.
For a single update, record its KB number and investigate the associated error.
If multiple updates fail, the problem may involve Windows Update services, connectivity, the component store or system configuration.
Check whether the computer is managed by Windows Server Update Services or organisational update policies.
Select the branch matching the failure pattern.

checkSpecificUpdate.title: Investigate the failing KB update
body: Record the exact KB number shown in Windows Update history.
Check Microsoft's Windows release health information for known installation problems.
Confirm that the update applies to the installed Windows version and architecture.
Check whether Microsoft has published an issue, workaround or replacement update.
If the update has a documented issue, follow that guidance.
Otherwise consider installing the specific update manually.

link.name: Microsoft: Windows 11 release health
link.description: Official Windows release information, known issues and resolved update problems.

link.name: Microsoft Update Catalog
link.description: Search for updates using their exact KB numbers.

waitForReplacementUpdate.title: Follow the documented update workaround
body: Microsoft has documented a problem affecting the specific update.
Follow the published workaround or resolution for the affected Windows version.
If the update has been withdrawn or superseded, use Microsoft's replacement guidance.
Continue installing unrelated supported updates where appropriate.
Check Windows release health for changes to the issue status.

link.name: Microsoft: Windows release health
link.description: Current known issues and officially documented Windows update resolutions.

manualInstallUpdate.title: Try installing the KB update manually
body: Open the Microsoft Update Catalog and search for the exact KB number.
Select the update matching the installed Windows version, architecture and package requirements.
Download the applicable standalone package.
Run the installer and record any error it reports.
Do not install arbitrary packages merely because they have a similar KB number.
For feature updates or unsupported package types, use Microsoft's recommended installation method instead.
If the update fails manually with the same error, continue with Windows Update diagnostics.

link.name: Microsoft Update Catalog
link.description: Official source for downloadable Windows update packages.

singleUpdateResolved.title: Update installed successfully
body: The update installed successfully using a standalone package.
Check Update history or the installed build to confirm the update is present.
The previous failure may have involved download or Windows Update delivery components.
Check for remaining available updates.
If failures continue with other updates, investigate the Windows Update services and component store.

checkPendingRestart.title: Check pending update operations
body: Check Windows Update for Restart required or pending installation messages.
Review whether another update or servicing operation is already in progress.
A pending restart can block subsequent installations.
If Windows is requesting a restart, allow it to complete before attempting further repairs.
Avoid interrupting firmware updates or an active Windows servicing operation.

restartComputer.title: Complete pending Windows servicing
body: Save open work and restart Windows to complete pending update operations.
Allow update configuration to finish without interrupting the process.
After signing in, check Windows Update history and retry the failed update.
If the same error returns, continue with storage and Windows Update diagnostics.

checkDiskSpace.title: Check available system drive space
body: Open Settings, System, Storage and check free space on the Windows system drive.
Windows Update requires space for downloads, extraction, installation and rollback files.
Feature updates can require considerably more space than small cumulative updates.
Compare the available capacity with Microsoft's requirements for the failing update.
If free space is insufficient, clean up unnecessary files before retrying the installation.

link.name: Microsoft: Windows Update troubleshooting
link.description: Official guidance covering insufficient storage and other update installation problems.

freeDiskSpace.title: Free space for Windows Update
body: Open Settings, System, Storage and review Temporary files.
Remove unnecessary temporary files and unused applications.
Review Downloads and Recycle Bin contents before deleting anything.
Consider moving large personal files to another suitable drive.
Avoid manually deleting Windows system folders or rollback files without understanding their purpose.
Retry Windows Update after recovering sufficient space.

link.name: Microsoft: Free up drive space
link.description: Official storage cleanup procedures for Windows.

runTroubleshooter.title: Run the Windows Update Troubleshooter
body: On Windows 11, open the Get Help application and search for Windows Update troubleshooter.
Follow its diagnostic steps and apply any recommended repairs.
Alternatively, open Settings, System, Troubleshoot, Other troubleshooters and run Windows Update where the option is available.
Review any reported problems or repair results.
Restart Windows if requested and retry the failed update.
If the troubleshooter does not resolve the issue, check the internet connection and update services.

link.name: Microsoft: Windows Update Troubleshooter
link.description: Official Windows 11 Get Help and built-in Windows Update troubleshooting instructions.

runTroubleshooter.alt: Windows 11 Other troubleshooters settings showing the Windows Update troubleshooter
runTroubleshooter.caption: Run the Windows Update troubleshooter to identify common installation and service problems.

checkInternetAccess.title: Check connectivity to update services
body: Check whether the computer can access normal websites and Microsoft services.
If other network applications are also failing, investigate the network connection.
For managed systems, check VPN, proxy, firewall, DNS and organisational update-server requirements.
A working browser does not guarantee that Windows Update endpoints are reachable.
If the update repeatedly fails during downloading, investigate network filtering or proxy configuration.
If connectivity is normal, continue with the Windows Update services.

link.name: Microsoft: Troubleshoot Windows Update
link.description: Official instructions for update download and connectivity failures.

useNoInternetGuide.title: Resolve the network or update-service connection
body: The computer cannot reliably reach the services needed for Windows Update.
If general internet connectivity is broken, use the No Internet Connection troubleshooting guide.
If internet access works but Microsoft update services are blocked, investigate DNS, proxy, VPN or firewall configuration.
On business computers, confirm the configured WSUS or other managed update source is accessible.
Retry Windows Update after correcting the connection problem.

checkUpdateServices.title: Check Windows Update services
body: Press Windows + R, enter services.msc and press Enter.
Locate Windows Update, Background Intelligent Transfer Service and Cryptographic Services.
Check whether the services are disabled, failing to start or reporting errors.
Some services normally use Manual or Trigger Start and do not need to run continuously.
Do not assume that a stopped service indicates a fault if its startup configuration is normal.
If a required service is disabled or failing, investigate its configuration.

link.name: Microsoft: Windows Update repair guidance
link.description: Official troubleshooting for Windows Update services and components.

restartUpdateServices.title: Repair Windows Update service operation
body: Identify the specific Windows Update service that is disabled or failing.
Check the relevant service error and configured startup type.
Restore an incorrect service configuration using Microsoft's documented settings.
Start or restart the affected service where appropriate.
Do not permanently set every update-related service to Automatic; Windows uses triggered services.
Retry Windows Update and record any service error that remains.

link.name: Microsoft: Troubleshoot update failures
link.description: Official procedures for Windows Update services and related failures.

checkSecuritySoftware.title: Check security or network software interference
body: Review antivirus, endpoint protection and firewall logs for activity matching the update failures.
Check whether a proxy, VPN or filtering product is preventing update downloads.
Look for confirmed blocked processes, files or Microsoft update endpoints.
On managed computers, consult the responsible administrator before changing security controls.
Do not disable endpoint protection merely to see whether updates start working.
If a specific security product is implicated, investigate its recommended configuration or available updates.

securitySoftwareIssue.title: Resolve confirmed security software interference
body: Identify the software or policy blocking Windows Update.
Check the vendor's support instructions for the relevant Windows version.
Correct the configuration or update the affected security application.
For managed systems, have the administrator approve policy or firewall changes.
Retry the Windows update after the confirmed interference is resolved.

resetUpdateCache.title: Rebuild the Windows Update download cache
body: Use this procedure if updates repeatedly fail to download or cached update files appear corrupted.
Open Command Prompt as administrator.
Run: net stop wuauserv
Run: net stop bits
Rename the existing download cache using: ren %SystemRoot%\SoftwareDistribution\Download Download.old
Run: net start bits
Run: net start wuauserv
Restart Windows and retry the failed update.
Windows will download required update files again.
If a rename fails because files are in use, follow Microsoft's full Windows Update component reset procedure rather than forcing deletion.
Do not delete the entire SoftwareDistribution or catroot2 folders without following the documented procedure.
Skip this step on managed computers unless the administrator approves it.

link.name: Microsoft: Reset Windows Update components
link.description: Official instructions for repairing update components and rebuilding update data.

checkSystemFiles.title: Check Windows component and system file integrity
body: Open Command Prompt or Windows Terminal as administrator.
Run: DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /ScanHealth
Review the result to determine whether component store corruption was detected.
Run: sfc /scannow
Allow the scan to finish and record whether corruption was found or repaired.
If Windows reports component store or system file corruption, continue with the repair procedure.
If no corruption is detected, investigate other update failure causes.

link.name: Microsoft: Repair Windows system files
link.description: Official reference for DISM and System File Checker diagnostics and repairs.

repairSystemFiles.title: Repair the Windows component store
body: Open Command Prompt or Windows Terminal as administrator.
Run: DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth
Allow DISM to complete; it may take several minutes or longer.
After DISM succeeds, run: sfc /scannow
Restart Windows and retry the failed update.
If DISM reports that source files could not be found, investigate a suitable repair source using Microsoft's instructions.
Do not repeatedly run repairs without reviewing persistent errors.

link.name: Microsoft: Use DISM and SFC
link.description: Official repair procedure, including alternative repair sources when Windows Update is unavailable.

checkDateTime.title: Check system time synchronisation
body: Check whether Windows displays the correct date, time and time zone.
An incorrect system clock can cause authentication and certificate validation problems.
Open Settings, Time & language, Date & time.
Check whether the clock is synchronising correctly.
On domain-managed computers, investigate the configured time source rather than changing it arbitrarily.
If the clock is correct, continue with storage and update log checks.

correctDateTime.title: Correct system date and time
body: Correct the Windows time zone and date settings.
Synchronise the system clock using an appropriate time source.
On domain-joined computers, confirm the domain time configuration.
Retry Windows Update and check whether the authentication or download error has cleared.

checkDiskHealth.title: Check system drive health
body: Use the drive manufacturer's diagnostic utility to check SSD or HDD health.
Review SMART information for media errors, critical warnings or reported failures.
Check Windows Event Viewer for repeated disk or storage controller errors.
Storage faults can prevent downloaded updates from being written or installed correctly.
If a storage fault is confirmed, prioritise protecting the data.
Do not replace a drive solely because an update failed.

replaceFailingDrive.title: System drive fault identified
body: Storage diagnostics indicate that the Windows system drive is unreliable.
Back up important files immediately if accessible.
Confirm the defective drive before replacement.
Replace the drive with a compatible device when required.
Restore Windows and personal files from a verified backup or reinstall the operating system.
Retry Windows updates after resolving the underlying storage problem.

checkEventLogs.title: Review Windows Update event logs
body: Press Windows + R, enter eventvwr.msc and press Enter.
Open Applications and Services Logs, Microsoft, Windows, WindowsUpdateClient, Operational.
Check events corresponding to the failed update's installation time.
Record the KB number, update title, error code and any recurring failure information.
For detailed component troubleshooting, open PowerShell and run: Get-WindowsUpdateLog
This command generates a readable WindowsUpdate.log file from update trace data.
For component store installation failures, also inspect CBS.log under C:\Windows\Logs\CBS.
Use these logs to identify the failing component rather than treating unrelated warnings as the cause.

link.name: Microsoft: Windows Update log files
link.description: Official reference for WindowsUpdate.log, CBS.log and other servicing logs.

link.name: Microsoft: Get-WindowsUpdateLog
link.description: PowerShell documentation for generating a readable Windows Update diagnostic log.

researchErrorCode.title: Investigate the recorded update error
body: Use the exact hexadecimal error code, update KB number and affected Windows build.
Search Microsoft's troubleshooting documentation for the specific failure.
Determine whether the error relates to component store corruption, permissions, downloading, applicability or another subsystem.
Check whether the error is known for the installed Windows version.
Use a documented repair that matches the evidence rather than repeatedly resetting unrelated components.
If a targeted repair is available, apply it and verify the outcome.

link.name: Microsoft: Windows Update troubleshooting
link.description: Official troubleshooting instructions for common update error codes and failures.

link.name: Microsoft: Windows Update logs
link.description: Technical reference for identifying update installation and servicing failures.

applySpecificFix.title: Apply the error-specific repair
body: Follow the Microsoft or manufacturer procedure matching the identified error.
Record any system settings or services that must be changed.
Apply the correction and restart if required.
Retry the failed KB update or installation.
If the same error remains after the targeted repair, investigate the Windows repair installation options.

repairInstallWindows.title: Repair Windows without removing applications
body: If Windows Update remains broken after targeted troubleshooting, consider a repair installation.
On supported Windows 11 systems, open Settings, System, Recovery.
Under Fix problems using Windows Update, select Reinstall now if available.
This reinstalls the current Windows version while preserving installed applications, files and settings.
The option may be unavailable on some managed devices or configurations.
Maintain reliable power and internet connectivity throughout the repair.
Back up important data and confirm access to any BitLocker recovery key before major repairs.
If this recovery method is unavailable or fails, investigate a supported in-place installation using Microsoft installation media.
A clean installation should be considered only after less-destructive recovery options have been assessed.

link.name: Microsoft: Fix problems by reinstalling Windows
link.description: Official Windows 11 recovery process that preserves applications, files and settings.

link.name: Microsoft: Recovery options in Windows
link.description: Compares repair, recovery, reset and Windows reinstallation methods.

repairInstallWindows.alt: Windows 11 System Recovery settings with Fix problems using Windows Update and Reinstall now highlighted
repairInstallWindows.caption: The Windows 11 repair option can reinstall the current Windows version while preserving apps, files and settings.

repairInstallResolved.title: Windows Update repaired
body: The Windows repair installation completed successfully.
Check Windows Update history and retry any remaining failed updates.
Confirm that applications and personal files are accessible.
Review Windows Update for additional required updates.
If the same problem returns, record the new error code and investigate the relevant servicing logs.

advancedWindowsRecovery.title: Further Windows recovery required
body: Windows Update remains unusable after component repairs and available Windows recovery methods.
Consider an in-place repair installation using official Windows installation media where supported.
Back up personal data and record installed applications before proceeding.
Check BitLocker recovery information, device drivers and the Windows edition before making significant changes.
For managed computers, follow the organisation's deployment and recovery procedures.
A clean reinstall is a last resort because it can remove applications, settings and personal data.
Retain the Windows Update error codes and servicing logs for further diagnosis.

link.name: Microsoft: Windows recovery options
link.description: Official recovery procedures including reinstalling Windows from installation media.
